title: How the Python SDK pages a list: has_next, next and the per-service branches

prose.text: One response object (`ZscalerAPIResponse`) pages every service, with a branch per service for how the next page is requested and when the walk stops. The branches are in each product's subject: [[zia.sdk-python.request-conventions:has-next-zia]], [[zpa.sdk-python.pagination]], [[zcc.sdk-python.pagination]], [[zidentity.api.pagination:python-next]], [[zdx.sdk-python.response-models:paging]], [[zscaler-cellular.api.wire-notes:sdk-paging]].

prose.label: Every service.
prose.text: {{next-is-get}} So a list fetched with POST (a search) cannot be continued with `next()`: [[zscaler-cellular.api.wire-notes:next-page-post-search]]. {{next-stopiteration}} {{next-empty-page}}

next-stopiteration.statement: `next()` raises `StopIteration("No more pages available.")` when `has_next()` is false, and otherwise returns the tuple (results, response, error).

next-empty-page.statement: `next()` raises StopIteration only when `has_next()` is already false; when the page it fetches is empty it returns None with no error instead.

next-is-get.statement: The SDK's next-page request is always a GET built from the response's URL, headers and query parameters (with the page advanced); the request it builds has no body key.

checks.do: Whether the list was fetched with POST before paging it with `next()`, which always sends a GET.
